glosses: A hammer powered by compressed air.

Something that is very strong but also very rigid.

examples.text: A new skiercross pro tour is on the docket, as well as freeskiing. Just like racing, both require strong but supple legs rather than jackhammer quads.

He was standing at a work table he’d jackhammered from a boulder, placidly sculpting a rose on its work surface.
[…] a bolt of lightning jackhammered across the sky, interrupting his dream.
When he jackhammered into her, she clutched the bedspread and braced herself for the onslaught.

glosses: To beat hard, to pound. (of the heart or pulse)

examples.text: […] he lay rigid, his heart jackhammering, telling himself that there was nothing out there, nothing […]

glosses: To strike (something) repeatedly with force, to pound.

examples.text: Guam-based B-52 bombers, newly modified to haul 60,000 lbs. of bombs each, jackhammered a Viet Cong radio and communications center 35 miles northeast of Saigon.

examples.text: Dans le silence, notre attention fut brusquement fixée par des trépidations lointaines qui allaient s’amplifiant sous les voûtes. On eût dit d’un marteau-piqueur manié par un ataxique.
